answer: Proof-of-replication forces each agent to cryptographically prove it stores a unique dataset replica before earning attestation rights. A beacon VRF seeds the challenge, so agents cannot pre-compute replicas. A jetty of verification nodes spot-checks random sectors; failed audits slash the agent's stake. The falcon signature scheme binds each proof to a single identity key, preventing replay across sybil clones. Replication costs grow linearly per identity, making mass cloning economically prohibitive.
